mainTopic: Finding the practical difference between 'כשר' and רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' for שבירת העצם, and the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about meat located elsewhere on the limb
overview: The word 'בו' in the פסוק forbidding שבירת העצם of the קרבן פסח can be read in two ways. One view limits the איסור to a כשר פסח. רבי limits it to a פסח that is ראוי לאכילה. The גמרא searches for a practical case where these two views give different results. One אמורא after another proposes a case, and the next אמורא rejects it: a פסח הבא בטומאה, a פסח once valid and then disqualified, breaking a bone by day, a limb that partly went outside, raw meat, the tail, and a bone with less than a כזית. The list ends with רבינא's case: a limb with no כזית at the break but a כזית elsewhere. A ברייתא of רבי is then shown to support four of these suggestions. Finally, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute רבינא's case. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא, and ריש לקיש's answer begins at the very end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First suggested difference: an impure פסח
steps.stepSummary: The end of the first answer: in a פסח הבא בטומאה, the 'כשר' view exempts it, while רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' view forbids breaking its bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is disqualified. According to the one who says the rule depends on being fit for eating, this one is also fit for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first proposed case that separates the two views: a קרבן פסח brought while the people are in a state of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'כשר' view, an impure פסח counts as פסול, so breaking its bones is permitted. Under רבי's view, the people who are allowed to bring it in טומאה may also eat it, so it counts as ראוי לאכילה, and breaking its bones is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן פסח brought in a state of טומאה, as is allowed when most of the community is impure
Disqualified, not valid
Fit to be eaten
According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The words 'הַאי פָּסוּל' are the end of the line 'according to the one who says כשר, this one is פסול.' The case being discussed is a פסח הבא בטומאה.

phrases.english: this one is disqualified.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the view of the one who says כשר: an impure פסח isn't valid, so there's no prohibition.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'fit for eating'
phrases.notes: This is רבי's view.

phrases.english: this one is also fit for eating.
phrases.notes: The impure people may eat it, so the prohibition applies.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה הַאי נָמֵי רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to 'מאי בינייהו', which was asked on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פסח הבא בטומאה: exempt under the 'כשר' view, forbidden under רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' view.

steps.title: רב יוסף rejects the impure-Pesach case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that everyone exempts an impure פסח, because רבי only came to add a leniency and never to add a stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: In a case like this, everyone agrees there is no prohibition of breaking a bone. רבי only came to be lenient, and this one is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says the impure פסח cannot be the difference, because both views agree that breaking its bones is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' rule was meant to exclude more cases, not to forbid cases the first view already permits. So רבי also accepts that a פסול offering has no איסור. Since a טמא offering is פסול, both views exempt it.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this
Everyone agrees
Breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח, which the תורה forbids
He comes to be lenient

steps.confusionAlert: רבי's rule is not a replacement for the 'פסול' exemption. It is an extra exemption added on top of it. Anything the first view exempts, רבי exempts too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the guiding principle for the rest of the sugya: a valid case of difference must be one where רבי is more lenient than the 'כשר' view, never stricter.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
In a case like this
phrases.notes: Meaning an impure פסח.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it is not subject to
the prohibition of breaking a bone,
because Rabbi comes only to be lenient,
phrases.notes: רבי adds an exemption. He does not remove one.

phrases.english: and this one is, after all, disqualified.
phrases.notes: So רבי also exempts it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case proposed in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the impure Pesach as the practical difference between the views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes רבי could be stricter than the 'כשר' view, but רבי only adds leniencies.

steps.title: רב יוסף's case: once valid, then disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests a פסח that was valid at first and later became disqualified. The 'כשר' view treats it as valid, but רבי says it is not fit for eating now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is an offering that had a time when it was valid and then became disqualified. According to the one who says 'valid,' this one is valid. According to the one who says 'fit for eating,' this one is not fit for eating now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers his own case that separates the two views. It fits his rule, because here רבי is the more lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'כשר' view, an offering that once had a שעת הכושר still counts as valid, so breaking its bones is forbidden. Under רבי's view, what matters is whether it can be eaten right now, and it cannot, so breaking its bones is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after rejecting the old one
A time when it was valid
And then it became disqualified
There is a difference between them
Valid

phrases.english: Rather, if it had a time of validity
and then became disqualified, that is the difference between them.
According to the one who says 'valid'
this one is valid.
phrases.notes: It had a time of validity, so the prohibition applies.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'fit for eating'

phrases.aramaic: הָא הַשְׁתָּא לָאו רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה הוּא.
phrases.english: now it is not fit for eating.
phrases.notes: So there is no prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר וְנִפְסַל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting step 1, רב יוסף offers a replacement case that fits his principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: היתה לו שעת הכושר ונפסל: forbidden under the 'כשר' view, permitted under רבי's view.

steps.title: אביי rejects רב יוסף's case
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that everyone exempts an offering that became disqualified, because right now it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In any case like this, everyone agrees there is no prohibition of breaking a bone. What is the reason? Now, at least, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says רב יוסף's case also fails, because both views would permit breaking the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under the 'כשר' view, what counts is the offering's status now. Its earlier valid moment does not help. Since it is פסול now, the 'כשר' view exempts it too, so the two views do not differ here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Now, at least

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that in any case like this
there is no prohibition of breaking a bone.
What is the reason?
Now, at least, it is disqualified.
phrases.notes: What counts is how it is right now, even for the one who says כשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's case from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'once valid, then disqualified' as the practical difference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a past moment of validity keeps the offering כשר, but its present status is what counts.

steps.title: אביי's case: breaking a bone while it is still day
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests breaking a bone during the day, before nightfall. The offering is valid then, but it cannot yet be eaten, because the פסח is eaten only at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, breaking a bone while it is still day is the difference between them. According to the one who says 'valid,' this one is valid. According to the one who says 'fit for eating,' now it is not yet fit for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own case that separates the two views: breaking a bone of the פסח before night arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the day the פסח is fully כשר, so the 'כשר' view forbids breaking its bones. But it may only be eaten at night, so under רבי's view it is not yet ראוי לאכילה, and the איסור does not apply yet. Here רבי is the more lenient one, which matches רב יוסף's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, before nightfall
Eligible to be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: There were three attempts to find the difference. (1) An impure פסח was rejected, because רבי only adds leniencies. (2) An offering that was once valid and then disqualified was rejected, because its present status decides. (3) Breaking a bone during the day is אביי's case: it is valid but not yet edible.

phrases.english: Rather, breaking a bone while it is still day
is the difference between them.
According to the one who says 'valid'
this one is valid,
phrases.notes: So the prohibition applies even by day.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'fit for eating'
now it is not yet fit for eating,
phrases.notes: It is eaten only at night. The sentence continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב יוסף's case, אביי offers a replacement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Breaking a bone by day: forbidden under the 'כשר' view, not yet forbidden under רבי's view.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי's ruling about thigh-bone marrow
steps.stepSummary: רבי rules that one may not sign up for a פסח just to eat the marrow of the thigh bone. If breaking a bone during the day were allowed, a person could break it in the day, take out the marrow, and sign up for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי says that people may sign up for the marrow of the head, but not for the marrow of the thigh bone. Why may they sign up for the head marrow? Because one can scrape it out and remove it without breaking a bone. Now, if you think breaking a bone while it is still day is fine, then let him also break the thigh bone during the day, take out its marrow, and sign up for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's suggestion from Step 5. It uses a ruling of רבי to show that breaking a bone during the day must also be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that according to רבי, breaking a bone during the day is allowed, because the meat is not yet fit to eat. But רבי says the thigh marrow cannot be counted on at all. That only makes sense if there is no permitted way to get it out, which means daytime breaking must also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: People sign up as members of a group for a קרבן פסח
Marrow (the soft inner part of a bone)
The thigh bone
While it is still day (before nightfall)

steps.confusionAlert: Signing up 'for the marrow' means joining a group in order to eat that part. You can only sign up for something you are actually allowed to eat. So the question is really: is there a legal way to get the marrow out?

phrases.english: They challenged: Rabbi says:
One may sign up for the marrow of the head
but one may not sign up for the marrow of the thigh bone.
For the marrow of the head, what is the reason?
Since he can scrape it out and remove it.
phrases.notes: He can take it out through the opening of the skull without breaking anything.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: that breaking a bone while it is still day is fine,
then the thigh bone too, let him break it while it is still day,
take out its marrow, and let them sign up for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case אביי proposed in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that according to רבי, breaking a bone during the day is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי forbids signing up for thigh marrow. That implies there is no permitted way to reach it, so breaking the bone during the day must be forbidden too.

steps.title: אביי answers: your logic would also allow burning the bone at night
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns the question around. Even at night one could burn through the bone with a coal, and burning is not 'breaking'. Yet רבי still forbids signing up, so the reason must be something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could answer you: By your reasoning, even after dark, let him bring a coal, put it on the bone, burn through it, take out its marrow, and sign up for it. For a ברייתא teaches: But one who burns bones or cuts sinews does not break the ban on breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by showing that the challenge proves too much. The same logic would also allow the marrow at night, through burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning a hole in the bone is not technically 'breaking' it, so by Torah law the marrow could be reached even at night. Since רבי still forbids signing up, his ruling must rest on some other reason. That means it cannot prove that daytime breaking is forbidden by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (turning the logic back on the questioner)
After it gets dark
A burning coal
One who burns bones
Sinews (tendons)

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:
And according to your reasoning, after dark as well:
let him bring a coal, place it on it, and burn it,
take out its marrow, and sign up for it.
For it was taught in a baraita:
But one who burns bones
or one who cuts sinews
does not violate the ban on breaking a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 by showing it proves too much
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-argument (ולטעמיך): the challenge's logic would also permit burning at night, so רבי's ruling must have a different basis
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי forbids thigh marrow because daytime breaking is forbidden by Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's ruling cannot prove anything about Torah law, because even burning at night is technically permitted

steps.title: Why burning the bone is still forbidden by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: Since burning is not breaking by Torah law, the ban on burning must be rabbinic. אביי says it is because the bone may burst. רבא says it is because the fire may destroy some holy marrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? אביי said: because the bone may crack open. רבא said: because of ruining holy food, since he actively ruins it, as the fire may consume some of its marrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי still forbids the thigh marrow at night: the Rabbis forbade burning the bone, and two reasons are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the heat may make the bone crack in another place, and that would be real 'breaking'. According to רבא, the fire may burn up some of the marrow, and it is wrong to destroy holy food with your own hands. Either way, the ban is rabbinic, not from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A burst or crack (the bone may split from the heat)
Ruining or wasting holy (sacrificial) food
Actively, with one's own hands
Fire

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
Abaye said: because it may burst,
Rava said: because of ruining holy food,
since he actively ruins it,
for perhaps the fire will consume some of its marrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the night-time ban raised in Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a rabbinic reason for the ban, with two competing explanations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the bone at night should be fully permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: Burning is forbidden by the Rabbis, either because the bone may burst (אביי) or because marrow may be wasted (רבא)

steps.title: Daytime breaking is banned only by a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: Breaking the bone during the day is also forbidden, but only by a rabbinic decree. The Rabbis feared that people would come to break bones at night too. So רבי's ruling does not disprove אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the day as well, it is a decree: daytime was forbidden because of after dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the defense of אביי. Daytime breaking is forbidden only to protect against breaking at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, אביי's case still stands: according to רבי, breaking during the day is allowed, because the meat cannot be eaten yet. The Rabbis forbade it anyway, so that people would not confuse day with night. That explains why רבי does not allow signing up for the thigh marrow.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a Torah violation
Because of (out of concern for)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי holds that breaking a bone during the day is permitted by Torah law but forbidden by a rabbinic decree. So אביי's case still works as the practical difference between the two views.

phrases.english: While it is still day as well,
it is a decree: daytime because of after dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם אַטּוּ מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of a rabbinic ban (Step 8) to daytime breaking, which fully answers Step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי's ruling about thigh marrow rests on rabbinic bans, so אביי's daytime case remains a valid difference by Torah law

steps.title: רב פפא rejects the daytime case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that everyone agrees breaking a bone during the day is forbidden, because the meat will be fit to eat that same night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In any case like this, everyone agrees the ban on breaking a bone applies. What is the reason? By evening it will be fit for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב פפא, rejects אביי's case from Step 5. Even רבי would forbid breaking during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fit for eating' does not have to mean fit at this very moment. A פסח that will soon be eaten at night already counts as fit. So daytime breaking is not a difference between the views.

keyTerms.meaning: Any case like this one
Everyone (all opinions agree)
In the evening, tonight

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְנָא —
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Any case like this,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם.
phrases.english: everyone agrees the ban on breaking a bone applies.
What is the reason? By evening it is fit for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proposed case from Step 5, even after it was defended in Steps 7-9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's case of breaking a bone during the day
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A פסח that will be eaten tonight already counts as 'fit for eating', so even רבי forbids breaking its bones

steps.title: רב פפא's case: a limb that partly went outside
steps.stepSummary: The real difference is a limb that partly went outside the permitted area. That part is still a piece of a valid קרבן, but it can never be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they disagree about a limb part of which went outside. The one who says 'valid': this is valid. The one who says 'fit for eating': this is not edible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own case where the two views lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part of the limb that went outside the permitted area is forbidden to eat forever, but the קרבן as a whole is still valid. The 'כשר' view therefore forbids breaking that bone. רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' view allows it, because that piece will never be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb part of which went outside its permitted area
They disagree
Something that can be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer of רב פפא: the views differ about a limb that partly went outside. It is part of a valid offering, so the 'כשר' view forbids breaking its bone. That piece will never be eaten, so רבי's 'ראוי לאכילה' view allows it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer works because the problem lasts forever. In the daytime case the meat soon becomes edible, but here the piece never will. That separates 'valid' from 'fit for eating' in a lasting way.

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about a limb part of which went outside.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר כָּשֵׁר — הָא כָּשֵׁר הוּא,
phrases.english: The one who says 'valid': this is valid,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה — הַאי לָאו בַּר אֲכִילָה הוּא.
phrases.english: and the one who says 'fit for eating': this one is not edible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בְּאֵבֶר שֶׁיָּצָא מִקְצָתוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the daytime case in Step 10, רב פפא offers his own case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference between 'כשר' and 'ראוי לאכילה' is a limb that partly went outside its permitted area

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports the Limb-That-Went-Out Case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that breaking a limb that partly went outside has no איסור of שבירת העצם. This fits the view that requires the meat to be ראוי לאכילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: if part of a limb went outside and someone broke it, that is not a violation of breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up step 11, which said the limb that partly went out is the difference between the two views. רבי ישמעאל rules there is no איסור, which matches the ראוי לאכילה view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the כשר view, that limb is still part of a valid קרבן, so breaking it should be forbidden. רבי ישמעאל says it is not forbidden. That means he holds the איסור only applies to meat that is ראוי לאכילה, and this limb can never be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
A limb that partly went out of its permitted area
The Torah איסור against breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
A limb that partly went out, and one broke it —
phrases.notes: Part of the limb left the area where the פסח may be eaten.

phrases.english: it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a תנאי source for the practical difference proposed in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the limb that partly went out is the case where the כשר and ראוי לאכילה views differ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who rules there is no איסור, following the ראוי לאכילה view.

steps.title: The Limb That Went Out Is Fully Disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says that in the case of the limb that went out, everyone agrees there is no איסור, because that limb is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת, son of רב אידי, said: in any case like this, everyone agrees there is no violation of breaking a bone, because this limb is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects the idea that the limb that went out is where the two views differ. He says both views agree there is no איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 treated that limb as still part of a valid קרבן that just cannot be eaten. רב ששת disagrees: once it went out, the limb itself is פסול. So even the כשר view has no איסור, and the case cannot show a difference between the views.

keyTerms.meaning: Any case like this
Everyone (all opinions agree)
Disqualified, invalid as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'פסול' with 'not fit to eat.' רב ששת's point is that this limb is worse than uneatable. It is not even valid, so both views exempt it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
Any case like this —

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם,
phrases.english: everyone agrees it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,
since this limb is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical difference of steps 11–12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the limb that went out shows a difference between the כשר and ראוי לאכילה views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The limb is פסול, not merely uneatable, so the כשר view also has no איסור.

steps.title: New Difference: Breaking a Bone of Raw Meat
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the real difference is breaking a bone while the meat is still raw. It is כשר, but raw it is not ראוי לאכילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is breaking a bone while the meat is raw. According to the one who says the rule is about a valid קרבן, this one is valid. According to the one who says it is about meat fit to eat, right now it is not fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the limb case, רב ששת gives his own case where the two views differ: a bone broken while the meat is still raw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw meat of the פסח is a perfectly valid קרבן, so the כשר view forbids breaking its bone. But the פסח may only be eaten roasted, so raw meat is not currently fit to eat. That is why the ראוי לאכילה view permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Raw (not yet roasted)
There is a difference between them
Valid as a קרבן
Now, at this moment

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם בְּנָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rather, breaking a bone while it is raw is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר כָּשֵׁר — הָא כָּשֵׁר הוּא,
phrases.english: The one who says 'valid' — this one is valid,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה — הַשְׁתָּא אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: and the one who says 'fit for eating' — right now it is not fit for eating.
phrases.notes: The פסח may only be eaten roasted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם בְּנָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the old case, רב ששת supplies a replacement practical difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement case (נפקא מינה) for the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The views differ over a limb that partly went out.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over a bone broken while the meat is raw.

steps.title: Raw Meat Can Still Be Roasted and Eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says raw meat does carry the איסור under both views, because it can simply be roasted and eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: any case like this is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone. Why? Because it is fit to eat, since one can roast it and eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects רב ששת's raw-meat case. He says both views would forbid breaking that bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'fit to eat' does not mean ready to eat this second. It means the meat can become edible. Raw meat only needs roasting, so even the ראוי לאכילה view counts it as fit, and the raw case shows no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for eating
He roasts it

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם,
phrases.english: Any case like this is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,
what is the reason? Because it is fit for eating,
since one can roast it and eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's raw-meat difference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The raw-meat case as the practical difference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Raw meat is still ראוי לאכילה because it can be roasted, so both views forbid breaking it.

steps.title: New Difference: Breaking a Bone in the Tail
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the difference is the tail (אליה). It is part of a valid קרבן, but it goes on the מזבח and is never eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, breaking the tail is the difference between them. According to the one who says 'valid', this is valid. According to the one who says 'fit for eating', this is not fit for eating, because the tail goes up to the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק proposes his own case where the views differ: breaking a bone in the tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אליה is burned on the מזבח, so no person eats it. It is still part of a כשר קרבן, so the כשר view forbids breaking it. The ראוי לאכילה view permits it, because it will never be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat tail of the sheep
It goes up to the Most High (burned on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rather, breaking the tail is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כָּשֵׁר — הָא כָּשֵׁר הוּא,
phrases.english: According to the one who says 'valid' — this is valid,
according to the one who says 'fit for eating' —
this is not fit for eating,
because the tail goes up to the Most High.
phrases.notes: It is burned on the מזבח as part of the אימורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שְׁבִירַת הָאַלְיָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected raw-meat case with the tail case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement case (נפקא מינה) for the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over the אליה, which is valid but goes to the מזבח.

steps.title: The Tail Is Certainly Not Eaten At All
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the tail certainly has no איסור of שבירת העצם, because it is not fit for eating at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a case like this certainly has no violation of breaking a bone, because it is certainly not fit for eating at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רב נחמן בר יצחק's tail case. He says it is obvious there is no איסור there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אליה is not food for people in any way, so it falls completely outside the איסור. Since it is not a real case of the איסור to begin with, it cannot serve as the difference between the two views.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly, definitely
At all

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא וַדַּאי אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם,
phrases.english: Any case like this is certainly not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא וַדַּאי אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַאֲכִילָה כְּלָל.
phrases.english: since it is certainly not fit for eating at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כָּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא וַדַּאי אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's tail case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The tail case as the practical difference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tail is not people's food at all, so it is clearly outside the איסור under every view.

steps.title: רב אשי's Difference: A Bone Without an Olive's Worth of Meat
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the difference is a limb with less than a כזית of meat on it. It is valid, but it lacks the minimum amount that counts as eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is a limb that does not have a כזית of meat on it. According to the one who says 'valid', this is valid. According to the one who says 'fit for eating', we need the minimum amount for eating, and it is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own case where the two views differ: a bone with less than a כזית of meat on it. The next step shows that רבינא rejects this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This bone is part of a כשר קרבן, so the כשר view forbids breaking it. The ראוי לאכילה view requires enough meat to count as halachic eating, which is a כזית. Without it, that view permits breaking the bone.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount for halachic eating
The minimum measure that counts as eating
And it is not there

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is over whether שבירת העצם depends on the קרבן being כשר or ראוי לאכילה. Each proposed difference was rejected in turn: the limb that went out (it is פסול), raw meat (it can be roasted), and the tail (it is never eaten). רב אשי proposes a bone with less than a כזית of meat. It is valid, but it lacks the שיעור of eating. רבינא rejects this case in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rather, a limb that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כָּשֵׁר — הָא כָּשֵׁר הוּא,
phrases.english: According to the one who says 'valid' — this is valid,
according to the one who says 'fit for eating' —
we require the measure of eating, and it is not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כַּזַּיִת בָּשָׂר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected tail case with the final proposed difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement case (נפקא מינה) for the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over a bone carrying less than a כזית of meat.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב אשי: under the ראוי לאכילה view, the איסור requires a כזית of edible meat, while under the כשר view it applies to any bone of a valid קרבן. רבינא rejects this in step 19.

steps.title: רבינא rejects the limb with less than an olive-size of meat
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says a limb with less than a כזית of meat has no איסור of שבירת העצם under both views, because a שיעור אכילה is always needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: In any case like this, there is no איסור of breaking a bone, because we need the minimum amount that counts as eating.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב אשי's case from Step 18. He says it cannot be the difference between the two views, because both views agree it has no איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the כשר view forbids breaking even a bone with less than a כזית of meat. רבינא answers that no one forbids it, since the איסור only exists where there is a real amount of eating. So both views give the same result, and this case does not separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: Any case like this
It does not carry the איסור of
The minimum amount that counts as eating (a כזית)

phrases.english: Ravina said:
any case like this
is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,
since we require the minimum measure of eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: כׇּל כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא לֵית בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's proposed difference from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the case of a limb with less than a כזית as the point where the two views differ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both views require a שיעור אכילה, so this limb is exempt under both and does not separate them.

steps.title: רבינא's difference: an olive-size of meat elsewhere on the limb
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a limb with less than a כזית at the spot of the break but a כזית elsewhere on it. It is forbidden under the כשר view and permitted under the ראוי לאכילה view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is a limb that does not have a כזית of meat in this spot but does have a כזית of meat in another spot. According to the one who says the rule depends on כשר, this limb is כשר, so it is forbidden. According to the one who says it depends on ראוי לאכילה, we need a שיעור אכילה at the spot of the break, and here there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers his own case where the two views really give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the כשר view, the limb as a whole has enough meat and comes from a valid קרבן, so breaking its bone is forbidden. Under the ראוי לאכילה view, the meat must be at the exact spot where the bone is broken. That spot lacks a כזית, so there is no איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: In this spot (where the bone is broken)
In another spot on the limb
This is the practical difference between them
At the place of the break

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 18. In רב אשי's case the whole limb has less than a כזית. In רבינא's case the limb has a כזית, just not at the spot of the break.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר
phrases.english: Rather, a limb that does not have an olive-bulk of meat
in this place

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בִּמְקוֹם אַחֵר
phrases.english: but has an olive-bulk of meat in another place
is the difference between them.
According to the one who says it must be valid,
this one is valid.
According to the one who says it must be fit for eating,
we require the measure of eating at the place of breaking,
and here there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּמָקוֹם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case that was rejected in Step 19 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case proposed as the practical difference between the views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference might have been a limb with less than a כזית in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is where the כזית sits: the כשר view looks at the whole limb, while the ראוי לאכילה view requires a כזית at the spot of the break.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי: the rule applies to a valid קרבן only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says a ברייתא supports four of the suggestions. It begins with רבי reading the פסוק as applying only to a כשר קרבן פסח, not a פסול one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with four of them. As it was taught: רבי says, "In one house shall it be eaten ... and you shall not break a bone in it." One is liable for a valid one, and one is not liable for a disqualified one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support and quotes its opening line, which sets the basic rule. This step prepares the specific cases that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בו ("in it") is read as limiting the איסור to a קרבן פסח that is כשר. A פסול one carries no איסור. The next lines of the ברייתא give cases that match specific suggestions from the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports four of them
"And you shall not break a bone in it" (שמות יב:מו)
One is liable for a valid one
Disqualified

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with four of them.
As it was taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּבַיִת אֶחָד יֵאָכֵל ... וְעֶצֶם לֹא תִשְׁבְּרוּ בּוֹ״,
phrases.english: "In one house shall it be eaten ... and you shall not break a bone in it,"
for a valid one he is liable,
and he is not liable for a disqualified one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּאַרְבְּעָה מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of suggestions ends, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports several of them.
steps.raayaObject: Four of the suggested differences between the views
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי on שמות יב:מו

steps.title: Once valid but disqualified at eating time: no prohibition
steps.stepSummary: A קרבן that was once valid but became פסול by the time of eating carries no איסור of שבירת העצם. This supports רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had a time when it was valid and it became disqualified at the time of eating, there is no איסור of breaking a bone in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a case that matches רב יוסף's earlier suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being valid at some earlier point is not enough. The קרבן must still be fit when it is being eaten. This matches the case רב יוסף gave for a שעת הכושר followed by פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when it was valid
It became disqualified at the time of eating

phrases.english: If it had a time of validity
and it became disqualified at the time of eating,
it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר וְנִפְסַל בִּשְׁעַת אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with its first specific case.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's case of a קרבן that was once valid and later became פסול

steps.title: The prohibition requires a minimum eating amount
steps.stepSummary: There is an איסור only where there is a שיעור אכילה. This supports רב אשי and רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has the minimum amount for eating, there is an איסור of breaking a bone. If it does not have the minimum amount for eating, there is no איסור of breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a rule about the minimum amount of meat. This supports רב אשי and רבינא, who both based their cases on the שיעור אכילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור needs a real amount of eating, a כזית. This is the idea behind רב אשי's case and רבינא's rejection and new case. Together with רב יוסף, these are among the four views the גמרא says the ברייתא supports.

keyTerms.meaning: It has the minimum amount for eating
It carries the איסור of breaking a bone

steps.whatToRemember: So far, the ברייתא of רבי supports רב יוסף (once valid, then disqualified) and רב אשי and רבינא (the שיעור אכילה). The next two clauses add support for רב נחמן בר יצחק and אביי.

phrases.english: If it has the measure of eating,
it is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone;
if it does not have the measure of eating,
it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בּוֹ שִׁיעוּר אֲכִילָה — יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a second rule, about the minimum amount. Two more clauses follow in steps 24-25.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי and רבינא, who require a שיעור אכילה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שיעור אכילה is required for the איסור of שבירת העצם.

steps.title: What is fit for the altar has no prohibition of breaking a bone
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a part fit for the מזבח has no איסור of שבירת העצם. This supports רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: That which is fit for the altar is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues reading the ברייתא it brought as support. This line backs up רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some parts of the קרבן פסח, like the אליה (tail), are burned on the מזבח and are not eaten. The ברייתא says breaking a bone in such a part is not forbidden. That fits רב נחמן בר יצחק, who said the difference between the views is the part that goes on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש
Fit for the altar, meaning a part that is burned on the altar rather than eaten
The fat tail of a sheep, which is offered on the altar

phrases.english: That which is fit for the altar
phrases.notes: For example, the tail (אליה), which is burned and not eaten

phrases.english: is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
phrases.notes: This supports רב נחמן בר יצחק

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרָאוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from steps 21-23 with another clause, which supports a third suggestion.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's view that the difference concerns a part offered on the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's clause: הראוי למזבח אין בו משום שבירת העצם

steps.title: The prohibition applies only at the time of eating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says breaking a bone is forbidden at the time of eating, but not at other times. This supports אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time of eating, it is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone. When it is not the time of eating, it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next line of the ברייתא. This line supports אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is eaten at night. אביי said the difference between the views is breaking a bone while it is still daytime, before eating time arrives. The ברייתא says the איסור applies only at the time of eating, which matches אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when the קרבן פסח is eaten, which is at night
While it is still day, before eating time

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports four suggestions. רב יוסף is supported by פסול after being valid. רב נחמן בר יצחק is supported by what is fit for the מזבח. אביי is supported by the time of eating. רב אשי and רבינא are supported by the שיעור אכילה.

phrases.english: At the time of eating
phrases.notes: At night, when the פסח is eaten

phrases.english: it is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone;
when it is not the time of eating
phrases.notes: For example, during the day

phrases.english: it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
phrases.notes: This supports אביי

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת אֲכִילָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת עֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the final supporting clause of the ברייתא. It completes the support for the suggestions.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the difference concerns breaking a bone before the time of eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's clause about בשעת אכילה versus שלא בשעת אכילה

steps.title: A dispute about a limb with meat only in a different spot
steps.stepSummary: A limb has no כזית of meat where it is broken, but it has a כזית elsewhere. רבי יוחנן says breaking it is forbidden, and ריש לקיש says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a limb has no olive-bulk of meat in this place, but it has an olive-bulk of meat in another place. רבי יוחנן said: it is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone. רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: it is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a disagreement between two אמוראים. It asks whether the meat has to be at the exact spot of the break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there must be a כזית of meat for the איסור to apply. The question is where that meat must be. For רבי יוחנן, a כזית anywhere on the limb is enough. For ריש לקיש, the כזית must be right at the place being broken.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb
In this place, meaning at the break / in another place on the limb

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here says a bone with no meat at all is forbidden. Both sides agree that a כזית is needed. They only argue about whether it must be at the exact spot of the break.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בִּמְקוֹם זֶה
phrases.english: A limb that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it in this place
phrases.notes: The spot where the bone is broken

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בִּמְקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: but has an olive-bulk of meat on it in another place,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
It is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: אֵבֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בִּמְקוֹם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new מחלוקת about the same type of case רבינא described in step 20: no כזית at the break, but a כזית elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: forbidden to break. ריש לקיש: permitted to break.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא. It says the פסוק forbids breaking both a bone with a כזית of meat and a bone without a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised an objection to רבי שמעון בן לקיש: 'And you shall not break a bone in it.' This applies both to a bone that has an olive-bulk of meat on it and to a bone that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins an attack on ריש לקיש by quoting a ברייתא. The גמרא is setting up the next move, which explains what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to forbid breaking even a bone 'without a כזית.' That sounds like it goes against ריש לקיש. However, the attack only works once we pin down what 'without a כזית' means, so the גמרא asks that next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall not break a bone in it.' This is the פסוק of the איסור
Both this... and that... A formula that includes two cases equally

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
'And you shall not break a bone in it' —

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עֶצֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: both a bone that has an olive-bulk of meat on it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד עֶצֶם שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: and a bone that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's position from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש, who permits breaking when there is no כזית at the spot of the break
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids breaking even a bone 'without a כזית,' which seems to include ריש לקיש's case.

steps.title: What does 'without an olive-bulk' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'without a כזית' means. It rejects the idea that it means no meat at all, because a bone like that cannot be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it' mean? If you say it has no olive-bulk of meat on it at all, why would it be subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what the ברייתא's words mean. It rules out the simple reading, which sets up the real meaning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya we learned that a שיעור אכילה is always needed. So a bone with no כזית anywhere cannot be forbidden. That means the ברייתא must be talking about some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: What? This asks for the meaning of a phrase
If you say. This introduces a reading that will be rejected
At all
Why?

phrases.english: What does 'does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it' mean?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא דְּאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר כְּלָל —
phrases.english: If you say that it has no olive-bulk of meat on it at all —

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם?!
phrases.english: why would it be subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone?!
phrases.notes: It is not fit to be eaten, so there should be no איסור

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 27 so the challenge can be sharpened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of 'a bone without a כזית' in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It cannot mean no meat at all, since a שיעור אכילה is required. The real meaning comes in the next step.

steps.title: The ברייתא means meat in another place, a difficulty for ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: So the ברייתא must mean a bone with no כזית at the break but a כזית elsewhere. Since the ברייתא forbids it, this is a קשיא on ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it is saying: both a bone that has an olive-bulk of meat in this place, and a bone that has no olive-bulk of meat in this place but has an olive-bulk of meat in another place? This is a difficulty for רבי שמעון בן לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only reading left for the ברייתא. It concludes that the ברייתא contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'without a כזית' must mean 'without a כזית at the spot of the break, but with a כזית elsewhere.' The ברייתא forbids breaking that bone, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's ruling. So ריש לקיש's view runs against a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? This introduces the forced reading
This is what it is saying
It is a difficulty

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן's reading of the ברייתא, a כזית anywhere on the limb is enough to forbid breaking the bone. This leaves ריש לקיש with a קשיא.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עֶצֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּמָקוֹם זֶה,
phrases.english: both a bone that has an olive-bulk of meat on it in this place,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּמָקוֹם זֶה
phrases.english: and one that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it in this place

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
phrases.english: but has an olive-bulk of meat on it in another place
— this is a difficulty for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rejection in step 28 to reach the only possible reading, which completes the challenge from step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids breaking a bone with no כזית at the break but a כזית elsewhere, which is exactly the case ריש לקיש permits.

steps.title: Opening the Response to the Challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a reply to רבי יוחנן's challenge from the ברייתא. Only the opening words of the reply appear here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is starting the reply to the קשיא from the ברייתא, and the actual answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 29, the ברייתא seemed to forbid breaking a bone that has no כזית at the break but has a כזית elsewhere. That was a problem for ריש לקיש, who permits it. 'He said to him' tells us ריש לקיש is about to defend his position.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer is already finished here. These two words only open the reply. You must keep reading into the next lines to see how the ברייתא is explained.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here comes the answer to רבי יוחנן's challenge. From the flow, the speaker is most likely ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the reply to the קשיא raised in Step 29 against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup only. The resolution itself appears on the next amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid breaking a bone with a כזית elsewhere but not at the break, which contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. This line only introduces the answer.
